edges.description: Loss of myl1 disrupts fast-fiber muscle structure and function, modeling the human fast-fiber defect.
edges.limitations: Transient morpholino knockdown in a non-mammalian embryo; fiber-type specialization and the chronic human disease course are not fully recapitulated.

nodes.description: Homozygous or compound-heterozygous loss-of-function variants in MYL1 (splice, nonsense, frameshift, deep-intronic splice-altering, or destabilizing missense) abolish or severely reduce production of the fast-skeletal myosin essential light chain, the structural light-chain component of fast-fiber myosin.

Loss of functional fast-twitch musculature manifests as severe congenital hypotonia and generalized weakness (including facial and respiratory musculature and reduced fetal movement), with respiratory insufficiency and feeding difficulties frequently requiring ventilatory and nutritional support.

nodes.description: Two of the four summarized individuals died in infancy (at 1 and 7 months) of respiratory failure. Recorded as an outcome; HPO files infantile death under Mortality/Aging rather than Phenotypic abnormality, so no HP term is bound.
